svg.aria-label: Scenario 9, crossing into a clinical study: the IRB protocol and consent form, drafted. You ask: We're crossing into a clinical study — write the IRB protocol and consent. A discipline card, a record: one file per field, core/disciplines/<field>.md, used when your overlay names one under ## Disciplines; it holds evidence conventions, terminology, what reviewers in the field ask, ethics and consent norms and a methodology switch, and every item carries a source; a model-written card enters as status: proposed with model provenance, and only the human operator moves it to accepted or rejected. No cards yet: research-master ships the card format only. Your overlay names the card under ## Disciplines. Step 1, /research-master:conductor runs the pipeline and passes the card's path into the briefs of the stages that touch the field; it never records an approval, signature or acceptance for you. Step 2, /research-master:research-mentor discusses the research, worn by the conductor and announced; it thinks with you, not for you, collaborative and Socratic, and restates the question and what decision hinges on it; it never asserts its own ideas as facts. On the way to drafting sits the sparring gate: it fires before advice that spends more than the project's compute threshold or changes a claim or the scope, at the design phase of a large plan, or when you and the mentor agreed a direction-level call within one exchange; pre-registrations keep their own gates, sparring is optional there; document mode hands premises to sparring-partner at the design phase of a large plan. When it fires, sparring-partner is dispatched across the context boundary with the proposal as written plus its evidence paths, never the mentor's own reasoning; it returns a verdict and the premise that decides it, each premise VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED or FALSE, a premise being VERIFIED only by a quote with file:line or by a command that was run and its output, and, if a check needs something unavailable, marked UNVERIFIED with the exact check that would settle it named; it is advice, never a veto, and never sees the proposer's reasoning. Its Independent audit — PROCEED, PROCEED-WITH-CHANGES or RETHINK, with the deciding premise — opens the mentor's answer; the audit advises, you decide. Step 3, /research-master:paper-writer, worn by the conductor and announced, in document mode drafts the IRB protocol and the consent form from your state files, in the template's own format, plus a source note. Rail a: template sentences are copied verbatim and only the template's own fields change. Rail e: register and length follow the template and, where your overlay names a card, what that card says the field's reviewers expect; with no card, the template alone. A field the state files cannot fill is left blank and listed as a question for you, never filled by guess. It never sends anything. Step 4, the draft is handed to you, and you read it in full before it leaves. Step 5, it is submitted after your full read; the submitted form follows its template. Footnote, from core/disciplines/README.md: A card advises a draft or a review; it never overrides SCIENTIFIC_RULES.md, a DECISIONS.md entry or a role's hard rules.
